hero.headline: Treasury moves to cut off crypto exchange MEXC from U.S. financial system over alleged $16 billion in illicit transactions
hero.teaser: The U.S. Treasury Department moved to cut off cryptocurrency exchange MEXC from the American financial system over allegations the platform processed $16 billion in illicit transac
hero.body:
The U.S. Treasury Department moved to cut off cryptocurrency exchange MEXC from the American financial system over allegations the platform processed $16 billion in illicit transactions linked to Iran, North Korea and Russia. The action targets MEXC Global for alleged sanctions violations.

The Treasury decision blocks MEXC from accessing U.S. financial infrastructure and conducting transactions with American counterparties. The enforcement measure represents one of the largest actions against a cryptocurrency exchange based on alleged illicit transaction volume.

The alleged $16 billion in flows involve transactions connected to sanctioned countries including Iran, North Korea and Russia. The Treasury did not specify the time period over which the transactions allegedly occurred or detail the nature of the illicit activity.

In response to the Treasury action, digital asset company NatGold Digital announced it would immediately delist its NATG token from MEXC. The move reflects the immediate market consequences for platforms cut off from the U.S. financial system.

cards.headline: House Republicans weigh impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth this week over alleged illegal continuation of Iran war
cards.body:
House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing Hegseth of defying Congress and illegally continuing the U.S. war in Iran. The political calculus shifted after Republicans suffered major losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, with defeated and retiring members now more willing to back impeachment against a defense secretary whose support has eroded since the Iran war began.

Speaker Mike Johnson had canceled votes and sent lawmakers home early before Election Day to avoid the politically difficult impeachment measure. Massie, who lost his Republican primary to a Trump-backed opponent, is now moving forward with the vote. Retiring Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska told reporters Hegseth does not have much support on Capitol Hill and said he remains undecided on the impeachment vote.

Republicans have blamed the Iran war for their electoral losses, with one lawmaker saying the party should never have pursued the war before the midterms. Another Republican told reporters that Hegseth's tone and rhetoric damaged the party's ability to explain why strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities and additional military actions were necessary. Some Trump administration officials have pushed for Hegseth's removal, though President Trump said Wednesday he intends to keep him in the post.

Hegseth called the impeachment effort a sham led by a disgruntled, defeated congressman. Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the Defense Department followed the law and that Hegseth will not be deterred by politicians seeking partisan points. Even if the House impeaches Hegseth, removing him would require a two-thirds Senate vote. Democrats, who will control the Senate in January after their midterm victories, would have the power to pursue their own investigations and impeachment proceedings if Hegseth remains in office.

cards.headline: Secret Service arrests man near White House with guns who said voices told him to kill Trump
cards.teaser: The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice
cards.body:
The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice

Officers approached Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos after observing him acting suspiciously in a parked car, according to a Department of Homeland Security statement. Chrinos described hearing voices instructing him to come to Washington and kill the president, the statement said.

cards.headline: Zelenskyy accuses Russia of escalating strikes on power grid to pressure Ukraine ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president says intensified attacks on energy infrastructure aim to weaken Kyiv's negotiating position at US-brokered trilateral meeting scheduled for next week.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of ramping up strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure to pressure Kyiv ahead of US-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week. Russia launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles overnight Saturday, triggering power outages across five regions, Zelenskyy said. He characterized the escalation as Russia perceiving diplomacy as a form of aggression.

Ukrainian and Russian negotiators are scheduled to meet with US envoys Tuesday and Wednesday in the first such talks in months. The diplomatic track stalled in February when Washington shifted attention to its war with Iran. Zelenskyy also urged the US to increase interceptor supplies for Patriot air defense systems.

cards.teaser: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government, giving the former military chief 28 days to build an administrati
cards.body:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government, giving the former military chief 28 days to build an administrati

Herzog announced the decision after consulting with political parties represented in the incoming Knesset, Israel's parliament. Eisenkot received 67 recommendations for the premiership compared to 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Artificial intelligence systems are now enabling attackers to automate the entire hacking process in real time, fundamentally disrupting the cybersecurity industry built over the p

Open-weight AI models have advanced to the point where they can automatically identify software vulnerabilities, write exploits, and break into targets simultaneously, collapsing what was traditionally a multi-step process requiring teams of skilled hackers. Stamos described a wave of breaches in recent weeks affecting major technology companies, including a chain of attacks that began with a compromise of Fireworks, an AI services provider.

hero.headline: Krakow gunman killed his parents and sister before Main Market Square attack that left six dead
hero.teaser: The three bodies found at the home of the 25-year-old gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday have been identified as his father, mother, and sister.
hero.body:
The three bodies found at the home of the gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday have been identified as his 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother, and 21-year-old sister, Polish police confirmed on Sunday. The 25-year-old Polish man drove into the square shortly before 15:00 local time and began firing at random people from his car, killing four women and two men including a British national before armed officers shot and arrested him within three minutes. A minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by far-right ideologies and described him as an ultra-nationalist.

Three of the six victims killed in the square are Polish and two have not been identified. Authorities discovered the three bodies at the suspect's home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city around 200 kilometers from Krakow, when they searched the residence after the attack. Sixteen people were taken to hospital, including five foreigners, two police officers, and the attacker. The local governor said the suspect remains in critical condition in hospital after undergoing surgery for a gunshot wound.

Police on Sunday named the two injured officers as Senior Constable Jakub Kulik and Senior Constable Artur Morański. One officer was described as being in very critical condition after being shot three times while detaining the gunman. In an update on Sunday, police said two women who were hospitalized following the incident had been released and the remaining individuals in Krakow's hospitals, including the two police officers, are in stable condition.

The attacker was wearing military-style attire and had a military-grade weapon, though authorities confirmed he was not a soldier. Police found multiple pieces of weapons and ammunition in his vehicle. Polish media reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home. A passing tram was shot at during the attack, shattering windows, though no passengers were injured.

The shooting occurred in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a popular tourist destination. Witnesses described hearing more than 20 shots from what sounded like multiple different firearms. Prime Minister Donald Tusk traveled to Krakow and said Poland had not previously experienced such drastic cases of terrorism. Krakow Mayor Åukasz GibaÅa declared a period of mourning in the city lasting until Wednesday.

cards.headline: Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh damaged after coalition intercepts Houthi missiles
cards.teaser: An administrative tower in the capital's financial district sustained damage from falling debris, with no casualties reported.
cards.body:
An administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh was damaged by falling debris after the Saudi-led coalition intercepted two missiles fired by Yemen's Houthis on Sunday, the kingdom's Energy Ministry said. Witnesses reported blown-out windows across several floors of the Aramco Tower in the King Abdullah Financial District, though no injuries or fatalities occurred.

The Houthis have increased missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, ports, and oil facilities since fighting resumed in July. An earlier attack on Riyadh's international airport in October killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, according to Saudi authorities. The escalation follows a day after Yemen's Houthi-run health ministry said Saudi airstrikes killed at least 33 people near Sanaa.

cards.headline: Putin expands state takeover of Japan Tobacco's Russian operations to seven companies worth up to $3.7 billion
cards.teaser: Moscow has seized three more subsidiaries of Japan Tobacco International, prompting a formal protest from Tokyo.
cards.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin placed three additional Japan Tobacco International subsidiaries under Russian-appointed management, expanding Moscow's takeover to seven companies with combined assets valued at up to $3.7 billion. The November 7 decree transferred control of JTI Russia, Pereslavl-Tabak, and JTI Innovative Products to the Russian company Industrial Assets, following a November 5 decree that seized four other JTI manufacturing and distribution businesses.

Japan has formally protested the seizures. Tokyo demanded Russia reverse the takeover, and Japan's Foreign Ministry raised the issue with Russian Ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev. JTI has operated in Russia since 1999 and previously controlled up to 40 percent of the country's cigarette market.

cards.headline: Drone attack on Colombian military base kills three soldiers and wounds 16
cards.teaser: The strike in Santa Rosa del Sur is the latest in a series of attacks on security forces as violence rises across rural Colombia.
cards.body:
A drone attack on a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur, northern Colombia, killed three soldiers and wounded at least 16, the armed forces said Saturday. Authorities did not identify who carried out the strike. The area is rich in gold mines and has been disputed by rebel armed groups including the Gulf Clan, the National Liberation Army, and smaller groups led by former Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia members.

Violence has intensified in rural areas since President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August and canceled peace talks with rebel groups. State forces and illegal armed groups carried out 34 attacks with bombs or explosives in Colombia in the four weeks to October 16, a 9 percent increase over the prior year's average, according to ACLED.

cards.headline: Cost-of-living protests spread to 31 European countries since mid-September
cards.teaser: More than 1,700 demonstrations have taken place across Europe, with France recording over 1,200 protests and riots.
cards.body:
More than 1,700 cost-of-living demonstrations have taken place in 31 European countries since mid-September, with France accounting for over 1,200 protests and riots, according to an analysis of Armed Conflict Location and Event Data. The protests, which began with French high school students protesting overcrowded classrooms and crumbling buildings, expanded to cover fuel prices, wages, and social housing.

Spain recorded 173 demonstrations, followed by Italy with 160 and Germany with 70. In Spain, tens of thousands rallied after parliament rejected emergency housing decrees in early October. United Nations experts expressed alarm in late October at what they called excessive use of force by French authorities, noting that almost a quarter of events in France were classified as riots.

cards.headline: BBC authenticates video of gunfire during Krakow attack that killed six
cards.teaser: Verified footage shows people fleeing and the moment shots were heard in Poland's main market square Saturday.
cards.body:
BBC Verify authenticated video footage showing the moments gunfire erupted during Saturday's attack in central Krakow that killed six people and injured several others. One video shows about a dozen people running inside two buildings before a black car with its front window open passes, followed by a police car. Another video captures the moment gunshots were heard in the city's main market square.

Polish authorities identified the suspect as a 25-year-old Polish citizen inspired by far-right ideologies who used military weapons. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three additional bodies were found at the suspect's home, which remains under search.

hero.headline: Wisconsin state trooper detained by ICE released under supervision after intervention by DHS secretary
hero.teaser: A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an air
hero.body:
A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an airport Thursday while attempting to visit his parents. Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe was released under an order of supervision following intervention by Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, according to his attorney.

Van Der Merwe entered the United States in 2019 at age 14 and attended high school in New Mexico, according to attorney Mark Christopher. His parents applied for asylum, and Van Der Merwe was granted work authorization while that process proceeded. He later attended the New Mexico Military Institute and sought to serve in the U.S. military but was not permitted because of his immigration status. Van Der Merwe began working as a Wisconsin state trooper in July 2025 and remains authorized to work in the country, Christopher said.

The Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that Van Der Merwe had legal permission to remain in the United States until September 2019 but overstayed his admission. The agency characterized the overstay as defiance of federal immigration law.

Christopher said the case was egregious and that he could not identify any public benefit from detaining Van Der Merwe. The trooper will remain under an order of supervision, with specific conditions to be determined within two weeks, according to his attorney.

A British citizen was among the four women and two men killed when the attacker drove onto Main Market Square, a popular tourist attraction in Poland's second-largest city, and began firing at people. Three of the dead were Polish and two have not been identified.

hero.headline: Musk says SpaceX could acquire legacy telecom carrier and use spectrum ten times more effectively
hero.body:
Elon Musk told investors on November 6 that SpaceX could acquire a legacy telecommunications carrier and use its airwaves ten times more effectively than current operators, though he named no target and no transaction has been filed. Musk made the comments by video at the Baron Investment Conference in New York, adding that any purchase would be conditional on SpaceX using spectrum better than the incumbent. Verizon and AT&T each declined 0.89 percent following the remarks, while SpaceX rose 8.62 percent to $134.27.

Deutsche Telekom chief executive Tim Hoettges said on a November 5 earnings call that SpaceX would need at least 200 billion euros, or roughly $220 billion, to compete with established U.S. carriers. Hoettges, whose company controls T-Mobile, estimated SpaceX holds 76 megahertz of spectrum compared with approximately 400 megahertz for T-Mobile, and said leasing tower space alone would cost $20 billion to $30 billion. He added that his company must still assume SpaceX will enter the market.

Any acquisition of a major carrier would require SpaceX to assume significant debt, including Verizon's $166.2 billion or AT&T's $159.6 billion, along with labor agreements, retail operations, and landline networks. Both antitrust regulators and the Federal Communications Commission would need to approve such a transaction. The three major carriers together were valued at approximately $507 billion, while SpaceX was worth roughly $1.77 trillion.

SpaceX purchased AWS-4 and H-block licenses from EchoStar in September 2025 for approximately $17 billion and has agreed to buy nationwide 800-megahertz licenses, with closing expected in the first half of 2027. Analysts noted that at its current price, SpaceX stock likely already assumes its Starlink Mobile service will succeed, and a carrier acquisition would add substantial debt and regulatory complexity to that assumption.

Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the trucks entirely or shift production elsewhere, but said the decision was to make room for building more of its self-driving Cybercab cars. Wes Morrill, the project's lead engineer, wrote on social media that Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab, appearing to suggest the vehicle is being discontinued.

cards.body:
A series of bomb threats targeting airlines and cyberattacks on critical infrastructure across Europe has disrupted everyday life and heightened security concerns, though the perpe

The incidents have affected multiple sectors, including aviation, healthcare, and food supply systems. Cyberattacks targeted European refrigeration systems and critical health infrastructure, including a French blood bank.

hero.headline: NASA opens astronaut applications to expand Artemis moon program
hero.body:
NASA announced Saturday that it is accepting applications for a new astronaut class to support its Artemis program, which aims to establish a permanent lunar base. The space agency made the announcement during an air show at Kennedy Space Center focused on lunar exploration and aviation technology.

Aspiring astronauts have until December 3 to submit applications. NASA expects to make its final selection by late 2027, with new candidates beginning training by early 2028. The timing aligns with NASA's plan to return astronauts to the lunar surface in 2028 after more than fifty years.

The recruitment comes as NASA faces a personnel shortage relative to its expanding mission. The agency currently has only 32 active astronauts. Its last astronaut call two years ago drew more than 8,000 applicants, with 10 making the final cut in September 2025. Artemis III commander Randy Bresnik said the agency has far more work than available astronauts as it works to expand human presence beyond low-Earth orbit. The Artemis II crew completed a lunar flyaround in April, launching the lunar campaign.

Candidates must be U.S. citizens with college degrees and professional work experience. The mandatory two years of training can be grueling, and astronauts may wait several additional years before flying to space. Artemis III astronaut Frank Rubio, who holds the U.S. record for consecutive days in space at 371, cautioned that going to the moon represents about one percent of an astronaut's work, with most time spent contributing to mission support. This will be NASA's 25th astronaut class since the original Mercury Seven in 1959.

cards.headline: NASA's Artemis II rocket disrupted ionosphere enough to interfere with GPS across North America, study finds
cards.teaser: Upper-stage burns created atmospheric disturbances that could have affected GPS signals, according to pre-print research.
cards.body:
A pre-print study found that NASA's Artemis II Space Launch System rocket disrupted Earth's ionosphere widely enough to interfere with GPS signals across North America. The rocket's second and third stage burns created ionospheric disturbances so large they could have sustainably disrupted GPS at the time of launch, while gravity waves traveled through the atmosphere across the continent.

The first stage had limited ionospheric impact because it burned at low altitude, but upper stages created increasing effects as the rocket moved through atmospheric layers. Researchers noted the ionospheric holes might become a concern as rocket launch frequency increases.

cards.headline: Physicists use trapped ions to simulate magnetic flux effect in particle physics model
cards.teaser: Oxford researchers demonstrated the Aharonov-Bohm effect in a lattice gauge theory using a quantum computer, a step toward simulating particle interactions beyond classical computing limits.
cards.body:
University of Oxford physicists used a trapped-ion quantum computer to simulate a lattice gauge theory in two dimensions, demonstrating how magnetic flux affects particle motion. The team used strontium ions' electronic states to represent gauge fields and their vibrations to encode matter particles, creating a closed loop where flux could be stored in entangled qubits.

In the experiment, particles tunneled freely between sites when flux was zero but remained frozen when flux was present, confirming the Aharonov-Bohm effect. The approach captures interactions between matter and gauge fields that earlier simulations could not, though the current single-loop system remains small enough for classical computers to solve. Researchers aim to scale to larger lattices that would exceed classical computing capabilities.

cards.headline: Kid-focused phones from Bark, Gabb, Pinwheel offer monitored alternatives to smartphones
cards.teaser: A growing market of devices restricts web browsing, social media, and app stores while giving parents control over contacts and screen time.
cards.body:
Companies including Bark, Gabb, and Pinwheel are selling phones designed specifically for children as parents seek alternatives to unrestricted smartphone access. The devices typically feature touchscreens and cameras but restrict or remove web browsers, social media, and app stores. Parents manage the phones through companion apps that approve contacts, monitor locations, set screen time limits, and in some cases alert to cyberbullying or explicit content.

The Bark Phone, built on Samsung hardware, starts at $240 plus a $29 monthly wireless plan and scans texts and photos for concerning content. Gabb phones eliminate online risks entirely with no browser or app store, starting at $159.99. Pinwheel devices begin at $119 and allow parents to create different usage modes throughout the day. Several companies also offer landline-style home phones for children.

hero.headline: Australia routs Samoa 44-12 to reach 16th straight Rugby League World Cup final
hero.body:
Australia dominated Samoa 44-12 at Sydney Football Stadium on Sunday to advance to a 16th consecutive men's Rugby League World Cup final. Reece Walsh scored three tries for Australia, who ran in eight total tries against a Samoa side undermined by errors and discipline issues. Australia will face New Zealand in the final in Brisbane next Sunday.

The match began with an intense confrontation during Samoa's ceremonial Siva Tau war dance, with players getting face-to-face with Australian opponents. Samoa took an early 3-0 lead when Stephen Crichton converted a penalty, but Australia quickly responded when Tom Dearden scored from a scrum. Australia added two more tries after Samoa discipline lapses gave them six-again advantages, with Jacob Preston and Tom Trbojevic scoring. Walsh added his first try and celebrated with a backflip, and Bradman Best scored before halftime to extend the lead.

Samoa's frustration grew as several refereeing decisions went against them. The most controversial came at the half-hour mark when Crichton appeared to have scored after Francis Manuleleua beat Walsh to a high ball, but replay review ruled Manuleleua had knocked on. Samoa's Spencer Leniu was sin-binned before halftime for speaking out of turn to referee Adam Gee. Samoa managed second-half tries from Crichton and Izack Tago, but Walsh responded quickly after both scores to maintain Australia's comfortable margin.

Australia, winners of the past three world titles, extended their dominance in the tournament. Walsh completed his first international hat-trick, and Bostock added a late try. Trbojevic's try was his eighth of the tournament, maintaining his position as joint-leading try scorer at the World Cup.

cards.headline: Messi wins second consecutive MLS Golden Boot, first player to do so
cards.teaser: Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi scored 26 goals in 31 appearances to claim the award for the second straight season.
cards.body:
Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's Sam Surridge. Messi also recorded 17 assists for a league-best 43 goal contributions.

The 39-year-old is the sixth player to win the award twice. Inter Miami finished 17 points behind Nashville in the Eastern Conference and will face Columbus Crew in the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs later this month.

cards.headline: Khawaja defends sandpaper scandal claims, says he didn't name teammates
cards.teaser: The retired Australian cricketer clarified his autobiography's assertions about the 2018 ball-tampering incident as Cricket Australia says it stands by its original findings.
cards.body:
Usman Khawaja said he has not thrown anyone under the bus with his autobiography's claims about the 2018 sandpaper scandal, which resulted in punishments for captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner, and opener Cameron Bancroft. In videos posted on Instagram Sunday, Khawaja said he never spoke on behalf of anyone else in his book despite media headlines, and argued the entire team should share collective responsibility for what happened in Cape Town.

Cricket Australia issued a statement saying all relevant information presented to date has been properly considered and it remains comfortable with the findings of its integrity process. Four bowlers from that Test—Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, and Nathan Lyon—previously denied knowledge of the plot in a 2021 joint statement.

cards.headline: Caroline Dubois seeks 2027 unification fight with Baumgardner-Turhan winner
cards.teaser: Britain's unified lightweight champion calls for title unification after Alycia Baumgardner faces Elif Nur Turhan for the IBF belt.
cards.body:
Caroline Dubois, the unified WBC and WBO lightweight world champion, says she wants to fight the winner of Sunday's bout between Alycia Baumgardner and Elif Nur Turhan for the IBF lightweight title. The 25-year-old British boxer plans to first face WBA champion Stephanie Han before pursuing the final belt in 2027.

Dubois described a potential fight with Baumgardner as women's boxing's next great rivalry and said she believes it could headline London's O2 Arena with all four world titles at stake. She will attend ringside Sunday to watch Baumgardner challenge Turhan and expects to call out the winner afterward.

cards.headline: Rangers extend unbeaten run to 12 matches but pundits question lack of clinical edge
cards.teaser: Rangers moved within a point of the Scottish Premiership lead with a 2-0 win over St Mirren, but manager and analysts say the team isn't playing to its full potential.
cards.body:
Rangers extended their unbeaten streak to 12 matches across all competitions Saturday with a 2-0 victory at St Mirren, moving within a point of the Scottish Premiership summit. Ryan Naderi scored from the penalty spot and Dan Neil added a deflected second, but the side created numerous additional chances without converting them.

Manager Derek McInnes and television analysts said Rangers lack a killer instinct despite their form. The team's expected goals total of 29.8 in 12 league matches far exceeds their actual 21 scored. McInnes acknowledged players need to make better decisions in the final third, while former striker Chris Sutton warned the lack of control will eventually cost them.

cards.headline: Willy Hutchinson upsets Joshua Buatsi to win WBC light-heavyweight title in Manchester rematch

cards.body:
Willy Hutchinson won the WBC light-heavyweight championship Saturday night in Manchester, defeating Joshua Buatsi by decision to avenge a loss from 2024. The judges scored the rema

The judges scored the rematch 117-112, 115-113, 115-113 in favor of Hutchinson, making the 28-year-old Scot the first British champion at the weight since Nathan Cleverly in 2017. The bout was elevated from an interim title fight to a full championship after American David Benavidez vacated the belt to move up to cruiserweight.

cards.headline: Oregon routs Ohio State 41-28, likely ending Buckeyes' playoff hopes with fake punt sparking turnaround
cards.teaser: Oregon defeated Ohio State 41-28 in Columbus, likely extinguishing the Buckeyes' College Football Playoff hopes and marking the first time Ohio State has suffered three or more los
cards.body:
Oregon defeated Ohio State 41-28 in Columbus, likely extinguishing the Buckeyes' College Football Playoff hopes and marking the first time Ohio State has suffered three or more los

The Ducks rallied from a 14-0 deficit to score 41 unanswered points after a fourth-down fake punt deep in their own territory completely shifted momentum late in the first half. Facing fourth-and-9 from their own 31-yard line while trailing 14-3, Oregon coach Dan Lanning called for a fake punt.

hero.headline: Godzilla Minus Zero heads toward $32 million opening weekend, surpassing predecessor's total domestic run
hero.teaser: Godzilla Minus Zero is tracking toward a $32 million domestic box office debut, far exceeding the full theatrical run of its 2023 predecessor. The sequel, which centers on postwar
hero.body:
Godzilla Minus Zero is tracking toward a $32 million domestic box office debut, far exceeding the full theatrical run of its 2023 predecessor. The sequel, which centers on postwar Japan dealing with attacks from the three-headed Ghidorah and the possibility of Godzilla's return, is outpacing Godzilla Minus One, which opened in December 2023 with $11.4 million and finished its domestic run at $57.1 million.

The film holds a 90 percent critics approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. The Hollywood Reporter chief film critic David Rooney called it a thrilling jolt of marauding monster action. Godzilla Minus One became Japan's first feature to win the Academy Award for best visual effects, adding $56.9 million internationally to its domestic total.

Warner Bros.' The Cat in the Hat opened in second place with $6 million domestically on Friday, including Thursday previews, from 4,003 North American locations. The animated film is projected to reach around $18 million for its opening weekend. The studio had initially projected a $20 million opening for the $92 million production and is hoping word of mouth will sustain the film through the Thanksgiving holiday and into December.

The Cat in the Hat, directed by Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni, earned an A CinemaScore from opening-weekend audiences. The film is an animated adaptation of the Dr. Seuss book.

cards.headline: SNL Weekend Update mocks Trump over midterm losses and Miller promotion
cards.teaser: Saturday Night Live targeted President Trump's response to Republican midterm defeats and his replacement of Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff.
cards.body:
Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update mocked President Donald Trump over Republican losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, which left Trump without GOP majorities in either chamber of Congress. Co-anchor Colin Jost joked about Trump's claim that he "tried hard" and "left it all on the field," saying Trump "failed concussion protocol" and could spend his remaining time "bejazzling the White House."

Jost also criticized Trump's Friday decision to replace chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller, predicting "things are going to get out of hand real quick." He compared the swap to "switching from wine to meth." The segment additionally featured an appearance by a cast member portraying Elon Musk discussing Republican campaign losses.

cards.headline: SNL's Weekend Update mocks Elon Musk over nearly $500 million spent on Republican Texas candidates
cards.teaser: The sketch featured Musk avoiding questions about his midterm losses after most Texas statewide races turned Democratic.
cards.body:
Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update featured a sketch mocking Elon Musk over his political spending in Tuesday's midterm elections. Actor Jeremy Culhane portrayed Musk attempting to avoid discussing the nearly $500 million he spent backing Republican candidates in Texas, where most statewide races turned Democratic.

Anchor Colin Jost highlighted the irony of Musk relocating to Texas from California to avoid Democratic governance and taxes, only to see Texas shift Democratic. The sketch included Musk's AI chatbot Grok delivering self-deprecating jokes at Musk's expense before the character left the desk.

cards.headline: King Charles' frustrated reaction to Caribbean downpour draws comparisons to Queen Elizabeth's composure
cards.teaser: Royal commentators analyzed the monarch's visible impatience after being left without an umbrella during a Nov. 1 rainstorm in Antigua and Barbuda.
cards.body:
Royal commentators analyzed the monarch's visible impatience after being left without an umbrella during a Nov. 1 rainstorm in Antigua and Barbuda.

King Charles threw his hands in the air and repeatedly waved at aides after being left without an umbrella during a heavy rainstorm at a Nov. 1 celebration in Antigua and Barbuda, while Queen Camilla was quickly sheltered.

cards.headline: Druski impersonates Elizabeth Holmes in SNL sketch parodying Nathan Fielder documentary
cards.teaser: The host played himself interviewing the Theranos founder in a fictional prequel to a real metadocumentary.
cards.body:
Saturday Night Live host Druski starred in a sketch imagining a fictional prelude to a Nathan Fielder metadocumentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes. In the sketch, Druski interviews Holmes, played by Jane Wickline, and her partner Billy Evans, played by Ben Marshall, expressing immediate skepticism about their behavior.

The sketch incorporated techniques from Fielder's documentaries, including reenactments. Druski portrayed himself finding someone to embody Holmes's character, then appeared as Holmes in an eerie exchange with the character. The sketch also featured Druski dismissing a product Holmes showed him and attempting to close her eyes during their interview.

cards.headline: Emma Stone surprises Druski during SNL monologue to discuss their upcoming film
cards.teaser: The Oscar-winning actress appeared during the comedian's hosting debut to discuss their collaboration in a Universal Pictures comedy.
cards.body:
Emma Stone made a surprise appearance during Druski's Saturday Night Live hosting debut monologue, joining the comedian to discuss their upcoming Universal Pictures comedy "The Catch." The film is directed by Stone's husband, Dave McCary, a former SNL segment director and writer.

During the exchange, Druski claimed he plays Stone's love interest in the movie, which Stone playfully corrected, saying they were not romantic interests in the film. Druski also told Stone he loved her in "Bugonia," adding that he wanted to be the first Black person to say so.

cards.headline: Thai director Thiti Srinuan says music-video revenue funded Taibaan Studio's 'Undertaker' franchise
cards.teaser: The filmmaker revealed how online content bankrolled the blockbuster series and described the studio's extreme commitment to on-set realism.
cards.body:
The filmmaker revealed how online content bankrolled the blockbuster series and described the studio's extreme commitment to on-set realism.

Thai director Thiti Srinuan said at Taiwan Creative Content Fest that Taibaan Studio funded its second, third, and fourth films with revenue from online music videos after the first film raised THB2 million. Srinuan's music videos have surpassed 4 billion combined views, and he negotiated revenue shares instead of flat fees.

hero.headline: House Republicans weigh impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth this week over alleged illegal continuation of Iran war
hero.body:
House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing Hegseth of defying Congress and illegally continuing the U.S. war in Iran. The political calculus shifted after Republicans suffered major losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, with defeated and retiring members now more willing to back impeachment against a defense secretary whose support has eroded since the Iran war began.

Speaker Mike Johnson had canceled votes and sent lawmakers home early before Election Day to avoid the politically difficult impeachment measure. Massie, who lost his Republican primary to a Trump-backed opponent, is now moving forward with the vote. Retiring Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska told reporters Hegseth does not have much support on Capitol Hill and said he remains undecided on the impeachment vote.

Republicans have blamed the Iran war for their electoral losses, with one lawmaker saying the party should never have pursued the war before the midterms. Another Republican told reporters that Hegseth's tone and rhetoric damaged the party's ability to explain why strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities and additional military actions were necessary. Some Trump administration officials have pushed for Hegseth's removal, though President Trump said Wednesday he intends to keep him in the post.

Hegseth called the impeachment effort a sham led by a disgruntled, defeated congressman. Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the Defense Department followed the law and that Hegseth will not be deterred by politicians seeking partisan points. Even if the House impeaches Hegseth, removing him would require a two-thirds Senate vote. Democrats, who will control the Senate in January after their midterm victories, would have the power to pursue their own investigations and impeachment proceedings if Hegseth remains in office.
